provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — drive-by redirects and exploit delivery are detectable at the victim via web-proxy/browser telemetry and IDS on anomalous redirects to attacker CDN-lookalike domains, though the injected code lives on third-party sites
medium — malicious attachments are detectable at the mail gateway and via document-spawns-script/child-process telemetry (Word/Excel spawning rundll32/powershell), though initial lure content varies
medium — links to newly-registered lookalike domains are detectable at mail/proxy layers via URL reputation and lookalike-domain analytics
medium — user opening a malicious document is detectable via office-application child-process creation and mark-of-the-web/enable-macro telemetry

high — rundll32.exe executing DLLs from unusual paths, with anomalous exports/command lines, or as a child of Office is a well-characterized, high-fidelity detection via process-creation and command-line telemetry
high — Empire/Cobalt Strike PowerShell exhibits characteristic encoded/downloader command lines detectable via script-block and module logging plus known-framework signatures

detection_candidates.technique_name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
detection_candidates.rationale: high — new service installation (Event ID 7045 / 4697) for an unsigned or anomalous binary is directly observable and high-fidelity, especially correlated with the TDTESS on-disk artifacts

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
detection_candidates.rationale: high — creation/modification of Run-key autostart values pointing to implant paths is directly observable via registry-modification auditing and autoruns baselining
high — scheduled-task creation is logged (Event ID 4698 / Task Scheduler operational); tasks launching payloads from user/temp paths are high-fidelity when baselined
medium — signed malware defeats naive signature trust, but signer reputation, certificate-transparency correlation and revoked/unusual-issuer analytics make it detectable in mature environments
medium — hidden-window flags (e.g. PowerShell -WindowStyle Hidden, ShowWindow SW_HIDE) are detectable in command-line and API telemetry but require correlation to reduce noise
medium — cross-process memory writes and remote-thread creation are detectable via EDR API telemetry, though injection is common and needs behavioral correlation
medium — registry writes to autostart/config locations are observable via registry auditing but blend with legitimate activity absent baselining
medium — abnormally long/high-entropy DNS labels and encoded payloads are detectable via DNS analytics and entropy heuristics

detection_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — lookalike/typosquat hostnames (alkamaihd, twiter-statics, cloudflare-statics, gstatic.online) resolving to non-CDN infrastructure are detectable via DNS/proxy analytics and ASN/reputation mismatch
high — process access to lsass.exe and Mimikatz signatures/command lines are highly observable via EDR process-access and image-load telemetry
medium — NBTScanner and NetBIOS sweep bursts are detectable via connection-fanout/east-west network analytics and known-scanner process signatures
medium — host-enumeration commands and NetBIOS resolution bursts are detectable in command-line/network logs but common; value from recon-burst process-lineage correlation

detection_candidates.technique_name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — archive-utility execution producing large/compressed outputs before egress is detectable via process command-line and file-write telemetry
medium — creation of archive files in staging directories preceding egress is detectable via file-write and access-pattern telemetry with baselining

medium — admin-share access (ADMIN$/C$), remote file writes and Type-3 logons (Event ID 5140/4624) are detectable via SMB and authentication telemetry, though they blend with legitimate administration

medium — DNS C2 is detectable via DNS analytics (high query volume to a single domain, abnormally long/high-entropy labels, TXT-record beaconing), but well-tuned DNS tunneling that mimics CDN nameserver traffic can blend — hunt-leaning candidate
medium — HTTP beaconing with basic-auth headers and Cobalt Strike default profiles is detectable via proxy/TLS-metadata and JA3/beacon-interval analytics, though maskable via malleable profiles
medium — encoded blobs in DNS labels/HTTP fields are detectable via entropy and pattern analytics on C2 channels
medium — downloads of secondary payloads following C2 contact are detectable via correlated network-fetch-then-file-write-then-execute telemetry
medium — proxying via lookalike infrastructure is detectable when the lookalike domains/ASNs are baselined and correlated with process activity, but generic proxying blends with normal traffic
medium — exfiltration over the existing C2 channel is detectable via outbound-volume anomalies on the C2 flow, though it hides within established beaconing

detection_candidates.technique_name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — DNS-tunnel exfiltration is detectable via per-domain query-volume, label-length and entropy analytics, but tuned tunneling that mimics CDN nameserver traffic can blend — hunt-leaning candidate

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — adversary domain registration is off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via passive DNS, newly-registered-domain and typosquat/lookalike monitoring against brand strings (akamai, cloudflare, gstatic, twiter, fbstatic)
low — compromise of third-party servers is off-victim from the perspective of the espionage target; intel/hunt candidate via web-defacement/injected-script monitoring on watched publisher sites
low — capability development is off-victim; intel candidate via malware-family clustering and code-reuse tracking
low — certificate acquisition is off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via certificate-transparency monitoring and code-signing-certificate reputation tracking
low — actor-controlled personas are off-victim; intel/brand-monitoring candidate
low — tool acquisition is off-endpoint; downstream tool use is where detection lands (intel/hunt candidate)
low — in-memory decode leaves little discrete signal; hunt candidate via memory forensics and payload-staging correlation
low — user-mode keylogging generates little discrete host signal; hunt candidate via implant behavioral correlation and hook/API telemetry
low — system-info queries are ubiquitous and low-signal; hunt candidate only within a tight recon-burst window
low — process enumeration is common and low-signal; hunt candidate via process-lineage correlation
low — screen capture generates little discrete signal; hunt candidate via implant behavioral correlation
low — local file collection is common; suspicious mainly via staging patterns and process-lineage context (hunt candidate)

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Custom Method
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — custom archiving leaves nonstandard artifacts that evade signature-based archive detection; hunt candidate via file-format/entropy analysis of staged output
